item.title: #3218381: #file_value_callbacks bypass the TrustedCallbackInterface protections
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +72/−7 · php +72/−7
  • Diff: ecc5d94
  • Discussion: #3218381 · 6 contributors · 24 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 6 contributors

Summary

The managed_file form element accepted #file_value_callbacks and called whatever was listed there, bypassing the trusted callback protections added in #2966327 to limit remote code execution through render arrays. Those callbacks are now checked the same way as other render callbacks. In Drupal 12.1 an untrusted callback still runs but triggers a deprecation. In Drupal 13.0 it will throw an exception. Custom and contrib code that uses #file_value_callbacks needs updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Closes a bypass of the trusted callback protections: arbitrary callables in #file_value_callbacks were executed unchecked.
  • Deprecation: Using #file_value_callbacks callbacks on managed_file that are not #[TrustedCallback]-tagged methods, TrustedCallbackInterface methods or anonymous functions is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will throw in drupal:13.0.0.

Technical details

ManagedFile::valueCallback() used to run $callback($element, $input, $form_state) for each entry in #file_value_callbacks. It now passes each one to StaticTrustedCallbackHelper::callback() with a custom message. That message says untrusted callbacks are deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and will throw in drupal:13.0.0, and it links to https://www.drupal.org/node/3620771. StaticTrustedCallbackHelper no longer supports a silenced deprecation (#3081025). The code therefore catches UntrustedCallbackException, calls @trigger_error($e->getMessage(), E_USER_DEPRECATED), and then still invokes the callback, which keeps the deprecation period working. The %%s in the sprintf() format is intentional: it leaves a %s placeholder for the helper to fill in with the callback. Trusted callbacks are methods tagged #[TrustedCallback], methods of a TrustedCallbackInterface class, and anonymous functions. Kernel test coverage was added in the file module's managed file element test. A comment on the issue notes that contrib has copied this pattern into other elements, and follow-up issues are probably needed for them.

Upgrade

Tag any #file_value_callbacks callback method with the attribute used in the core test:

use Drupal\Core\Security\Attribute\TrustedCallback;

#[TrustedCallback]
public function managedFileValueCallbackTrusted(array &$element, $input, FormStateInterface $form_state): void {
  // ...
}

Alternatively, implement TrustedCallbackInterface on the class or use an anonymous function. Plain function names such as 'die' are no longer trusted. They trigger a deprecation in 12.1 and will throw in 13.0.

item.title: #3398033: Fix deprecated assert.active directive
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +11/−6 · php +6/−4 · htaccess +5/−2
  • Diff: e180d54
  • Discussion: #3398033 · 15 contributors · 66 comments
  • Followers: 32
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 15 contributors

Summary

The scaffolded .htaccess no longer sets the assert.active PHP directive, which is deprecated in PHP 8.3 and can log a deprecation under Apache with mod_php. It now sets zend.assertions to 0 (assertions compiled in but skipped). Comments recommend 1 on development machines and 0 or -1 in production. The fix was committed to main and backported to 12.0.x, 11.x, 11.5.x, 11.4.x, 11.3.x and 10.6.x. Release managers said it needs a release note because it changes a scaffolded, site-owner-managed file.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Scaffolded .htaccess now sets php_value zend.assertions 0 instead of php_value assert.active 0.

Technical details

The .htaccess template (php_value assert.active 0 inside <IfModule mod_php.c>) is replaced with php_value zend.assertions 0, plus a comment pointing to the PHP manual. The header comment is reworded to say the block is for PHP settings that cannot be changed at runtime. The docblock in default.settings.php is also updated. It now says to set zend.assertions=1 in php.ini on development machines and 0 or -1 in production, with a @see link to the PHP manual. It no longer claims the setting cannot be changed from .htaccess.

Background from the thread: #3375693 removed the assert_options() calls and the assertion-enabling code in example.settings.local.php. It left assert.active 0 in .htaccess. Under Apache with mod_php, that value still takes effect. A settings.local.php that only sets zend.assertions therefore could not turn assertions back on. Using zend.assertions in .htaccess restores the documented way to enable them.

The thread notes that zend.assertions can only be fully enabled or disabled in php.ini. If php.ini sets it to -1, the .htaccess line can trigger a PHP warning in the Apache log. Participants suggested that such sites remove the line or ignore the warning. A related question, whether tests should force assertions on, was split off to a gitlab_templates issue (3500234).

Upgrade

Existing sites keep their current .htaccess, because it is a scaffolded file. To pick up the change, update the block manually or re-scaffold:

<IfModule mod_php.c>
  php_value zend.assertions 0
</IfModule>

If your PHP config sets zend.assertions to -1, you can remove that line.

item.title: #3471113: Update to selenium/standalone-chrome:134+
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +17/−1 · php +14 · yml +3/−1
  • Diff: 9faf7e2
  • Discussion: #3471113 · 7 contributors · 60 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Core's FunctionalJavascript tests now run against a current Chrome in CI (pinned to 155.0 in the commit on main, previously 133.0) instead of an old one. Since Chrome 134, a WebDriver click could return before the page navigation had started, so tests randomly read the old page. Core's Selenium driver now turns off the Chrome feature behind this. Local, CI and contrib test runs that use Drupal's driver get the fix, with no test changes needed. This does not change site runtime behavior.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The cause is Chrome's DeferRendererTasksAfterInput feature, on by default since Chrome 134. It delays some page tasks until the next frame after an input event. DrupalSelenium2Driver::setDesiredCapabilities() is now overridden to append --disable-features=DeferRendererTasksAfterInput to goog:chromeOptions args before calling the parent. Putting the flag in the driver, not in .gitlab-ci.yml, means it applies to every runner, including contrib and local ones.

.gitlab-ci.yml gets a new SELENIUM_CHROME_TAG variable, set to "155.0". The .with-selenium-chrome service now uses selenium/standalone-chrome:$SELENIUM_CHROME_TAG, and the job that runs with COMPOSER_UPDATE: "1" overrides the tag to latest. The issue text proposed 152.0, but the diff pins 155.0.

CKEditor5AllowedTagsTest::testFullHtml() is now skipped with markTestSkipped(). Newer ChromeDriver treats zero-height elements as not displayed, which exposed empty filter tips under text format selectors. That is tracked in #3621903.

The issue notes that Chromium has not formally shipped this feature, so a later Chrome may remove the flag. The alternative was waiting for two animation frames after each click and form submit. It costs about 30 ms per click, so it was not chosen. It is being explored separately in #3631249 for the remaining random failures. Related earlier discussion: #2909782 and #2936122.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 30, 2024
  • Committed: October 16, 2026 (2 years later)

Key contributors

  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • graber (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • herved (European Commission and European Union Institutions, Agencies and Bodies)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

mstrelan opened the early attempts, which tried to add waits after pressButton, and then built a proof of concept that waited for two animation frames. herved found the Chromium root cause, DeferRendererTasksAfterInput, and later got the flag working in MR !16675 after longwave's first attempt showed no effect. graber built an in-driver wait alternative (MR !16706) and measured about +7% test time for it. graber then argued for setting the flag in DrupalSelenium2Driver instead of .gitlab-ci.yml, so it applies to all test runners. mstrelan agreed that disabling the flag beat the "nasty" workaround. The wait approach was kept as a follow-up, #3631249, for the random failures that remain.

item.title: #3029364: "None" Argument Validator for Views Contains an Undefined Variable
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Minor bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +43/−1 · php +43/−1
  • Diff: c8ac3d2
  • Discussion: #3029364 · 7 contributors · 30 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

The "None" contextual filter validator in Views lost a numeric check years ago. A cleanup removed the check because it referenced an undefined variable. The check is back. For a numeric argument handler where break_phrase is not set in the options, a numeric value now passes validation. A non-numeric value still fails. Before the fix, every value failed in that case. The fix was backported to 12.0.x, 11.x and 11.5.x as a low-risk bug fix.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Drupal\views\Plugin\views\argument_validator\None::validateArgument() originally came from the procedural validate_argument_basic($arg). When it was moved into a method taking $argument in #1788266, the is_numeric($arg) check kept the old variable name. #3316276, a PHPStan "undefined variable" cleanup, then removed the check as unused. Without it, the condition !empty($this->argument->definition['numeric']) && !isset($this->argument->options['break_phrase']) returned FALSE for any value.

The merged change restores the check using the real parameter: && !is_numeric($argument). It also adds the unit test Drupal\Tests\views\Unit\Plugin\argument_validator\NoneTest. The test covers numeric and non-numeric values, the break_phrase bypass, and the null and empty cases with and without must_not_be.

item.title: #2879023: Batch is dependent on the order of query string parameters
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +78/−2 · php +72 · js +6/−2
  • Diff: 2c6cf43
  • Discussion: #2879023 · 23 contributors · 117 comments
  • Followers: 46

Summary

Batch operations that run through the browser progress bar no longer break when a CDN or reverse proxy sorts query string parameters (Cloudflare "Query String Sort" and Fastly were reported). Before, the batch requests ended in a 406 "Not acceptable format: json" error and larger batches did not finish. The fix was backported to 11.4.x and later. Sites that worked around this with a page rule disabling query string sorting for /batch* can drop that rule after updating.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The initial batch URI already contains op=do_nojs. core/misc/batch.js appended a second op to it (&op=do for polling, &op=finished at the end). A proxy that sorts parameters alphabetically moved op=do_nojs last. PHP then used that value, so _batch_page() took the do_nojs branch for a _format=json request and returned an HTML render array, which triggered the 406.

The shipped fix is client side. batch.js now builds a URL from batch.uri and calls url.searchParams.set('op', ...) for both the do polling URL and the finished redirect, so each request carries exactly one op. An earlier approach (MR !15103, merged server side) treated do_nojs on non-HTML requests as do in _batch_page(). It was dropped because the duplicate parameter comes from Drupal's own JavaScript, so fixing it at the source was preferred. Both approaches got manual confirmation on Cloudflare.

The no-JS meta refresh path is unchanged. A FunctionalJavascript test (testBatchUrls) uses a new batch9 in the batch_test module. It checks that each polling request URL ends in /batch?_format=json&id=1&op=do and that the finished URL ends in /batch?id=1&op=finished.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 17, 2017
  • Committed: October 17, 2026 (9 years later)

Key contributors

  • hideaway
  • blacklabel_tom (Reason Digital)
  • dawehner (Chapter Three (acquired by Kanopi Studios))
  • rbayliss (Last Call Media)
  • bvoynick (Interactive Strategies)
  • nicxvan
  • john cook (Creode)
  • y.sa
  • m4olivei
  • dries
  • eduardo morales alberti (Metadrop)
  • doka

Collaboration

The issue ran from 2017 to 2026, with many people confirming it on Cloudflare and Fastly. For years the proposed fixes patched the request handling. Dries first proposed a server-side correction (treat do_nojs on non-HTML requests as do) and tested it on his Cloudflare site. alexpott then argued the fix belonged in batch.js, which is the code that adds the duplicate op, and supplied the URL.searchParams.set() change and a test. Dries reviewed it, preferred it to his own approach, and confirmed it on his Cloudflare site. That version was the one committed.

item.title: #3513035: Add constraint to check that the max delta for a field item list does not exceed its cardinality
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +287/−0 · php +283 · yml +4
  • Diff: 20ac0fa
  • Discussion: #3513035 · 12 contributors · 77 comments
  • Followers: 15
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 12 contributors

Summary

Field storage config validation now rejects a cardinality lower than the number of values already stored for that field. Before, validation could not catch this. Setting cardinality to 1 on a field where some entity already holds 2 values now fails with a message like "The field 'field_int' of entity type 'entity_test' has more entries (2) than the cardinality (1) allows." Unlimited cardinality (-1) is always accepted. The change landed in main, and later comments record backports to 11.x and 11.5.x. It also unblocks the parent effort #3324140 to convert field storage and field config form validation into validation constraints.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: field.storage.*.* config schema: cardinality now carries the NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinality constraint.
  • New API: New NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinality validation constraint plugin (with entityType and fieldName options) in the field module.

Technical details

The constraint is a plugin class, Drupal\field\Plugin\Validation\Constraint\NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinality. It was originally named NoEntitiesExistYetWithHigherCardinality and was renamed because it counts field items, not entities. It takes entityType and fieldName options. field.storage.*.* in field.schema.yml wires it to the cardinality key using %parent.entity_type and %parent.field_name.

NoFieldItemsExistWithHigherCardinalityValidator resolves those expressions with TypeResolver::resolveExpression() and skips validation in three cases:

  • The cardinality is unlimited.
  • The field_storage_config entity doesn't exist yet.
  • The storage has custom storage (hasCustomStorage()).

Otherwise it runs an aggregate entity query with MAX on field_name.%delta, with access checks off. It adds 1 to the result, because deltas start at 0, and adds a violation if that count is greater than the cardinality. An early version compared the raw max delta, which allowed two extra values. This was caught when a test was added that actually calls the validator.

The kernel test expects a SchemaIncompleteException when FieldStorageConfig::save() is called with the lowered cardinality. A unit test covers the constraint's defaults and message. The constructor uses explicit typed properties instead of the base Constraint option handling, because of the Symfony 7.4 deprecations (#3555534). Per the thread, the main commit has no exception handling in the validator, and the backport adds #[HasNamedArguments] and a catch for the exception that occurs in tests.

  • Committed: May 11, 2026 (1 year later)

item.title: #3571580: add a generic bundle type entity delete form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +239/−173 · php +239/−173
  • Diff: a7c1655
  • Discussion: #3571580 · 10 contributors · 61 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 10 contributors

Summary

Core now has a generic delete form for bundle entities (content types, block types, media types, comment types and so on). If any content of that bundle exists, the form says so, hides the Delete button and keeps a Cancel button, which non-JS users need on the standalone page. Node, block content, media and comment types now use it. Their separate copies of this logic are gone, so the wording of the "you can't delete this" messages changes slightly. For example, nodes are now described as "content items" instead of "pieces of content". Contrib bundle entity types can use the same form instead of writing their own.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: The delete forms for node, block content, media and comment types now render the blocking message and a Cancel button, built from the entity type labels. Markup and message wording differ from before.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Entity\Form\BundleEntityDeleteForm, a generic delete form for bundle entity types, with overridable getContentEntityCount() and getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion().

Technical details

Drupal\Core\Entity\Form\BundleEntityDeleteForm extends EntityDeleteForm. In buildForm() it reads getBundleOf() from the bundle entity type and throws a \LogicException if the type is not a bundle of anything. It then counts content entities of that bundle via getContentEntityCount(), using an entity query with accessCheck(FALSE) on the content entity type's bundle key. It also collects strings from getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion(), which returns an empty array by default. If either blocks deletion, the form shows each reason as a paragraph, changes the title to "Unable to delete @bundle-label %type", and returns only the actions element with submit removed. Otherwise it defers to the parent form. The messages use the singular and plural labels of both entity types, so a bundle entity type should define label_singular and label_plural for itself and for its content entity type to get good wording.

CommentTypeDeleteForm now extends this class. It overrides getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion() to report comment fields that still use the comment type. The @internal classes NodeTypeDeleteConfirm, BlockContentTypeDeleteForm and MediaTypeDeleteConfirmForm were deleted. The delete form handler on NodeType, BlockContentType and MediaType now points to BundleEntityDeleteForm. Tests in entity_test gain labels and edit-form and delete-form links for entity_test_bundle, plus a kernel test BundleDeleteFormTest. A follow-up commit fixed that test's namespace from Drupal\FunctionalTests\Entity to Drupal\KernelTests\Core\Entity.

The issue discussed a "delete all content" option, as Paragraphs offers. It was left out of scope. Core's DeleteMultipleForm does not yet support bundles, so this would need a follow-up.

Upgrade

Contrib bundle entity types that hand-roll a "can't delete while content exists" form can switch to the generic one in their entity type attribute:

use Drupal\Core\Entity\Form\BundleEntityDeleteForm;

handlers: [
  'form' => [
    'delete' => BundleEntityDeleteForm::class,
  ],
],

To add extra blocking conditions, extend it and override the method, as CommentTypeDeleteForm does:

protected function getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion(): array {
  $reasons = parent::getAdditionalReasonsToPreventDeletion();
  $reasons[] = $this->t('...');
  return $reasons;
}

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 4, 2026
  • Committed: October 16, 2026 (8 months and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • joachim
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

During review, berdir pointed out that Paragraphs lets admins delete the leftover content from the bundle delete form. longwave suggested keeping the "additional reasons" method separate from counting content entities, and joachim adopted that split in the final design. Deleting the content itself was left for a follow-up. quietone's usability review led to removing the trailing period from the form title, and she wrote a second change record with screenshots. joachim explained why the Cancel button stays alongside the modal's close control: without JS the form is a standalone page with no modal close control.

item.title: #3114467: 'Negate' form value for condition plugins should be cast to boolean in validation.
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +128/−53 · php +128/−53
  • Diff: 65625de
  • Discussion: #3114467 · 24 contributors · 63 comments
  • Followers: 40
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 24 contributors

Summary

The "negate" option on condition plugins (for example "Show for the listed pages") is now saved as a true boolean instead of 0/1 from a checkbox. Config entities that use condition plugins outside the block UI, such as Google Tag containers when the moderation dashboard is enabled, could previously end up with a wrongly typed value and stop showing. Those forms no longer need to cast the value themselves.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

ConditionPluginBase::validateConfigurationForm() was an empty method. It now calls $form_state->setValue('negate', (bool) $form_state->getValue('negate')), so the value is cast before submitConfigurationForm() copies it into $this->configuration['negate']. The config schema declares negate as boolean, but checkbox form elements submit 0/1. Core's BlockForm::validateVisibility() already did this cast for blocks only; other forms embedding condition plugins had to repeat it. The diff does not remove the BlockForm cast, though the issue suggested it could go.

The change landed after a first commit was reverted from main, because its unit test broke pipelines under newer PHPUnit mocking. The shipped version adds ConditionPluginBaseTest, a data-provider unit test that uses a small concrete TestConditionPluginBase class instead of a mock builder. It checks that 0, 1, '0', '1', '', FALSE and TRUE all end up as strict booleans. Related: #2815829 casts config values by schema at a lower level on form submit, but the thread found it did not fix this case.

Upgrade

Sites that applied a local patch for this issue can remove it after updating core. Config entities already saved with a non-boolean negate (for example a Google Tag container) need to be re-saved through their form so the value is stored as a boolean. This is based on comments in the thread, not on the diff.

item.title: #3627629: Remove search module coverage from robots.txt
item.description:

Summary

Sites that move to the contributed Search module and want to keep crawlers out of search results must add the rules back to their own robots.txt.

item.title: #3594335: Add a module and theme uninstall command
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +580/−38 · php +579/−38 · txt +1
  • Diff: 3b94128
  • Discussion: #3594335 · 9 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 14
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Drupal core now has an ex:uninstall console command (aliases exun, pm:uninstall, pmu) that uninstalls modules or themes from the command line. It takes a comma-separated list of machine names. It lists the extensions it will remove, including dependents pulled in automatically, and asks for confirmation before removing the dependents. --yes skips the prompt and --dry-run shows what would happen without changing anything. It is the counterpart to the ex:install command, as part of the CLI in Core initiative.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Both installer interfaces gained a new abstract method, so custom implementations of ModuleInstallerInterface or ThemeInstallerInterface must implement it.
  • New API: ModuleInstallerInterface::getModulesToUninstall() and ThemeInstallerInterface::getThemesToUninstall() resolve the full, ordered set of extensions an uninstall would remove.

Technical details

The command is Drupal\Core\Extension\Command\ExtensionUninstallCommand, marked @internal. It classifies each name as a module or theme, reports unknown names, and refuses to mix modules and themes in one invocation. It resolves the full set through the new getModulesToUninstall() or getThemesToUninstall() method. For modules it then runs validateUninstall(), the same checks as the uninstall form, and reports blockers before changing anything. In non-interactive mode, extra dependents without --yes throw UserAbortException.

To make this possible, the dependency resolution that used to sit inside ModuleInstaller::uninstall() and ThemeInstaller::uninstall() was extracted into the two new public interface methods. getModulesToUninstall() returns the installed modules to remove, including installed dependents when $uninstall_dependents is TRUE. They are sorted by module weight, the order uninstall() uses. It throws UnknownExtensionException for unknown modules or dependents. ModuleInstaller::uninstall() still returns FALSE in those cases, so its behavior for callers is unchanged.

getThemesToUninstall() throws for themes that are not installed, the default theme and the admin theme. With $uninstall_dependents TRUE it adds installed sub-themes to the list. ThemeInstaller::uninstall() passes FALSE, so it still throws if a base theme's sub-theme is not listed explicitly. ModulesUninstallConfirmForm::buildForm() now also calls getModulesToUninstall(), so the confirmation list includes dependents in uninstall order.

Upgrade

Custom classes implementing ModuleInstallerInterface or ThemeInstallerInterface must add the new methods:

public function getModulesToUninstall(array $module_list, bool $uninstall_dependents = TRUE): array;
public function getThemesToUninstall(array $theme_list, bool $uninstall_dependents = TRUE): array;

item.title: #3613347: Re-use container in kernel tests
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +180/−41 · php +180/−41
  • Diff: 6868135
  • Discussion: #3613347 · 4 contributors · 27 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Kernel test classes that share their environment (via the ShareEnvironment attribute from #1411074) now build the container once for the first test method and load it from cache for the remaining methods. Test classes that don't share the environment behave as before for container building. In the author's measurements, a 26-method test went from about 19s to about 15s. With xhprof enabled, per-method time dropped from about 2.5s to about 700ms. The saving is smaller for tests that install modules in several methods.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: KernelTestBase::$container is now typed ?ContainerInterface instead of ?ContainerBuilder; KernelTestBase::$keyValue is now the booted container's keyvalue service rather than a memory factory.
  • New API: New @internal Drupal\Core\Test\KernelTestDrupalKernel and a protected DrupalKernel::getContainerFromCacheIfCacheable() hook.

Technical details

KernelTestBase::bootKernel() now creates a Drupal\Core\Test\KernelTestDrupalKernel (marked @internal) instead of a plain DrupalKernel, passing static::sharesEnvironment() as the cache flag. When the environment is shared, it calls setContainerNeedsRebuild(FALSE) and setOverrideUseCache(TRUE), so the first method compiles and caches the container and later methods load it. To support this, DrupalKernel::initializeContainer() now calls a new protected getContainerFromCacheIfCacheable(), which holds the old "module list not set and no forced rebuild" check, and the subclass overrides it. The subclass appends a cacheSuffix to getContainerCacheKey() and increments it in rebuildContainer() and resetContainer(). A container rebuilt inside a test method is therefore cached under its own key and does not overwrite the initial one. bootKernel() calls resetCacheSuffix() and then resetContainer(), so every method starts from the same cached initial container with fresh service state. There is an @todo pointing at #2218651.

KernelTestBase no longer registers its own synthetic keyvalue service (memory factory, or database factory for shared environments). The container's normal key value service is used, and $this->keyValue is set from $this->container->get('keyvalue') after boot. As a result the key_value table now exists in kernel test databases. Core tests were adjusted: SchemaTest expected table lists now include key_value, a menu link content test lists key_value among its tables, and the installer test drops key_value in setUp() so the installer sees an uninstalled site. $container is now typed ?ContainerInterface. A new KernelTestSharedContainerTest uses the container_rebuild_test module's counter to assert the container is built once across three data-provider iterations. Follow-ups were opened for sharing caches between methods (#3629052) and deprecating KernelTestBase::$keyValue (#3629287). The PhpDumper container work in #3583505 is expected to be compatible with this approach.

Upgrade

Core tests that inspect the database table list needed key_value added, for example in SchemaTest:

$this->assertEquals(['config', 'key_value', 'select'], $tables);

Contrib kernel tests that type-hint $this->container as ContainerBuilder or assume an in-memory $this->keyValue may need adjusting. In the issue thread the committer expected existing tests to keep working and planned to update the shared-environment change record (https://www.drupal.org/node/3623403) with conversion steps.

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core

Summary

Drupal core's dr command line tool gains a config:export command. It writes the site's active configuration into the configured sync directory, matching what the Configuration UI export produces. It shows a table of what will be created, updated, deleted or renamed, and asks for confirmation unless --yes (-y) is passed. If the sync directory already matches, it reports that and does nothing. This is part of the CLI in Core initiative (#3582246) and is useful for deployment workflows and keeping config in source control.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New config:export console command (Drupal\Core\Config\Command\ConfigExportCommand, marked @internal) run via dr config:export, with a --yes/-y option.

Technical details

ConfigExportCommand is registered with #[AsCommand(name: 'config:export')] and autowires the config.storage.export service, the same export storage the UI uses. Because of that, config overrides (such as $config settings overrides) are not exported, and export transformers (for example from config_transformer_test in the tests) are applied. It also takes the SyncFactory service. The sync storage is resolved inside __invoke() rather than the constructor. SyncFactory::get() throws ConfigDirectoryNotDefinedException when no sync directory is configured, and a throwing constructor would break dr list for every command. The command catches that exception, prints the message and returns FAILURE.

A StorageComparer between export and sync storage builds the changelist. With no changes it prints a success message and exits. Otherwise renderTable() prints Collection, Config and Operation columns, with renames shown as old -> new. After confirmation the command calls replaceStorageContents() from StorageCopyTrait, which replaces the sync contents with the export. Declining the confirmation throws UserAbortException. A kernel test, ConfigExportCommandTest, covers the missing directory case, --yes, the no-changes case, cancelling, and transformers being applied. A PHPStan baseline entry was added for the missing return type on replaceStorageContents().

item.title: #3575642: Always free up old container on rebuild, not only in the installer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +62/−19 · php +62/−19
  • Diff: 7336168
  • Discussion: #3575642 · 7 contributors · 30 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 7 contributors

Summary

Rebuilding the service container, for example when modules are installed or uninstalled during update hooks, used to keep the old container and everything it referenced in memory. Core already fixed this for the installer only. It now applies on every rebuild. The reporter saw an update that installs and uninstalls several modules grow to 666MB. With the change it stayed at roughly 300MB or less. Sites that hit the error You have requested a synthetic service ("kernel") when modules with injected hook classes (such as pathauto) were enabled also reported that the merge request fixed it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: DrupalKernel::attachSynthetic() now resets the previous container, and Container::reset() and PhpArrayContainer::reset() keep synthetic services (and request_stack) instead of clearing everything. The InstallerKernel::attachSynthetic() override is removed.

Technical details

DrupalKernel::attachSynthetic() now calls $this->container?->reset() on the previous container after attaching synthetic services to the new one. This replaces the override that previously lived only in InstallerKernel, which is deleted. The old reset() simply emptied $services. Calling it on every rebuild would have dropped synthetic services such as kernel and keyvalue, which can't be built by the container. That is what caused the synthetic service exceptions in tests. Container::reset() and PhpArrayContainer::reset() now clear private services and unset only non-synthetic services, and they always keep request_stack. request_stack is not synthetic but must not be reset. PhpArrayContainer checks the synthetic key in the definition, which may be a serialized string. Container checks isSynthetic().

Because the old container is now reset, objects that outlive a rebuild can no longer rely on it. ModuleInstaller::updateKernel() records the service IDs of its uninstallValidators through ReverseContainer::getId() before the rebuild. Afterwards it replaces them with a RewindableGenerator that fetches the same services from the new container. MimeTypeGuesser::registerWithSymfonyGuesser() moves from DrupalKernel::preHandle() to initializeContainer(), so Symfony's static MIME guesser is re-registered with the new container on each rebuild. In the thread, the concern was that this call is on the early critical path before a page cache hit. Following up by adding MimeTypeGuesser to the early bootstrap autoload classmap was deferred to #3612177. The diff also includes a comment update in a router installer test.

Upgrade

Custom code that caches services in properties across a container rebuild, such as module installs or updates inside one request, may now hold services from a reset container. Re-fetch them from \Drupal::getContainer() after the rebuild, as ModuleInstaller::updateKernel() now does for its moduleHandler, connection, updateRegistry and uninstallValidators. Tests that persist services with injected dependencies, such as event dispatchers registered via register(), may need adjusting.

Summary

Database query objects (Select, Insert and so on) can no longer be serialized or unserialized on the main branch (12.x). Attempting it now throws a LogicException. On 11.5.x the same methods were deprecated rather than removed, so custom or contrib code that serializes a query, or an object holding one, gets a deprecation notice there and should stop. Core itself does not do this anywhere.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Query::__sleep() and Query::__wakeup() removed in 12.x; Query serialization and unserialization now throw \LogicException (deprecated in 11.5.0 on the 11.x branches).

Technical details

Query::__sleep() and Query::__wakeup() are replaced in Drupal\Core\Database\Query\Query by __serialize() and __unserialize(), which both throw \LogicException. The old __wakeup() reattached an unserialized query to whatever connection Database::getConnection($this->connectionTarget, $this->connectionKey) returned at the time, with no guarantee that connection was the right one. This was inconsistent with Connection, which already refuses serialization (#2463321), and with PDO. The change also finishes off #2463321. The now-unused Database import is removed. The commit landed on main and 12.0.x as a hard removal. On 11.x and 11.5.x it landed as a deprecation, with the deprecation version being 11.5.0 and removal in 12.0.0, pointing to change record https://www.drupal.org/node/3625908. I only read the main diff, so the 11.5.x deprecation details come from the reviewer comment on MR !17239. #3548971 (replacing __sleep()/__wakeup() with __serialize()/__unserialize()) is the related issue, and this change means Query no longer needs converting there.

item.title: #1411074: Allow kernel tests to share the test environment
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 36 files, +1261/−145 · php +1261/−145
  • Diff: 47430c3
  • Discussion: #1411074 · 23 contributors · 138 comments
  • Followers: 47

Summary

Kernel test classes can now opt in to sharing one database across all their test methods with the #[ShareEnvironment] attribute. The schema, config and other initial state are built once per class instead of once per method, which speeds up classes with many methods (the issue reports roughly 20 to 40 percent of total time). Classes without the attribute behave exactly as before. In core, the config entity validation tests were converted as the first users. Converting the rest of core's Kernel tests, and later making sharing the default in the next major, are follow-ups. The change was also backported to 11.x and 11.5.x so contrib can adopt it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ConfigEntityValidationTestBase now builds its entity in setUpEnvironment() and reloads it in setUp() for shared classes. Core subclasses were converted from setUp() to setUpEnvironment().
  • New API: New Drupal\TestTools\Attribute\ShareEnvironment attribute, plus KernelTestBase::setUpEnvironment(), resetEnvironment() and sharesEnvironment().

Technical details

The attribute is not inherited: ShareEnvironment::isEnabledFor() reflects on the concrete class only, and #[ShareEnvironment(FALSE)] marks a class as needing its own environment. For an opted-in class, a #[BeforeClass] hook (allocateSharedDatabase()) reserves one database prefix with a locked TestDatabase and passes it to the forked per-method processes through the DRUPAL_TEST_SHARED_DB_PREFIX environment variable. An #[AfterClass] hook drops all the tables and releases the lock. PHPUnit's #[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses] is still in effect, so each method still has its own process, container and virtual file system. Only database state is shared.

In bootKernel() the first method calls the new setUpEnvironment() hook (empty by default), then records the table list and a ready row in a test_shared_database_state table. Later methods skip the hook. If the hook fails, or a method breaks the shared state, the state is marked invalid and the remaining methods fail with the recorded reason. For shared classes the keyvalue service is a KeyValueDatabaseFactory instead of the in-memory factory, so entity definitions and state persist with the tables. core.extension is rewritten per method with the module list rebuilt but the installed themes kept.

The old tearDown() table-dropping logic moved to resetEnvironment(), which does nothing for shared classes. Instead tearDownEnvironment() fails the method if it dropped a shared table or left a new table behind. INFRASTRUCTURE_TABLES (currently cache_container) is exempt, and a class can redeclare it. Test methods must not assume a clean database, and tables they create must be removed in resetEnvironment(). ConfigEntityValidationTestBase was adapted: shared subclasses build $this->entity in setUpEnvironment(), and the base setUp() records and reloads the entity from the key value store. Unconverted subclasses that assign $this->entity in setUp() still work. A change record is at node 3623403, and follow-ups are #3623409 (add the attribute to all Kernel tests) and #3623410 (make sharing the default). #3613347 (re-use the container) builds on this.

Upgrade

To opt a Kernel test class in, add the attribute and move fixture creation from setUp() to setUpEnvironment(), as the converted core tests do:

use Drupal\TestTools\Attribute\ShareEnvironment;

#[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses]
#[ShareEnvironment]
class ActionValidationTest extends ConfigEntityValidationTestBase {

  protected function setUpEnvironment(): void {
    parent::setUpEnvironment();
    // Build the shared fixture here.
  }

}

Remove tables or other state a test method adds by overriding resetEnvironment() and calling the parent.

item.description:

Summary

Three response subscribers no longer trigger "Passing null to parameter #1 ($haystack) of type string is deprecated" when a response carries a Content-Type header whose value is NULL. This showed up as unsilenced deprecations in PHPUnit runs (for example the Gatsby module's kernel test), as image generation problems for a site using a webp convert effect, and as failing contrib tests such as JSON:API Extras. Anonymous access to a Views data export that required authentication also triggered it. Those responses are now skipped by the subscribers, as any non-matching content type would be.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

HeaderBag::get('Content-Type', '') returns NULL, not the default, when the header exists with a [null] value, so the '' default did not protect stripos() and str_contains(). The fix changes the call to $response->headers->get('Content-Type') ?? '' in ActiveLinkResponseFilter, RssResponseRelativeUrlFilter and the JSON:API ResourceResponseValidator. The root cause, discussed in the thread, is that Request::getMimeType() returns NULL when the format is not registered in Request::$formats. Drupal normally registers formats in NegotiationMiddleware::handle(). The JSON:API, REST and serialization subscribers then call headers->set('Content-Type', NULL). Response::prepare() cannot repair this because it only acts when the header is absent. Tightening those writers was left for a follow-up, since it would change behavior (no header versus an empty one). Tests were added: ResourceResponseValidatorTest::testOnResponseNullContentType() and an ActiveLinkResponseFilter unit test that promotes E_DEPRECATED to an exception.

item.title: #3626105: Release runtime theme registries after destruction
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +26/−1 · php +26/−1
  • Diff: 96cfe41
  • Discussion: #3626105 · 4 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 7
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

On persistent PHP workers such as FrankenPHP in worker mode, the theme registry service can outlive a request. After the first request's cleanup, later requests could log "Theme hook %hook not found." and render nothing for the affected hooks. The registry now discards its runtime collectors during cleanup, so the next request gets fresh ones and theme hooks are found again. Sites on classic PHP-FPM or Apache are not affected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Registry::destruct() called destruct() on each collector in $this->runtimeRegistry but kept them. CacheCollector::destruct() persists pending changes and resets storage. Registry::getRuntime() then returned the same retained, emptied ThemeRegistry, whose has() and get() read that storage directly. So previously registered hooks came back as missing, and ThemeManager::render() logged the "not found" message and returned FALSE.

The fix copies $this->runtimeRegistry to a local variable, sets the property to [], then destructs the copies. The next getRuntime() call builds a new ThemeRegistry, whose constructor loads the runtime cache or initializes on a miss. Repeated destruct() calls also skip collectors that were already processed. A new kernel test, testRuntimeRegistryAfterDestruct() in RegistryTest, checks that a hook is still found after destruct() and that a different collector instance is returned. The committer noted that for persistent workers it may be better not to clean up these collectors at all, so a loaded registry stays available across requests. That is left for later work.
